Welcome toExtinguishers on a Beam

Two extinguishers on a level beam — slide one along it. What changes, and what doesn’t?

Listen to the intro

About: Same two extinguishers, one beam

Source

Collection
Wieman mechanics simulations — Introductory Mechanics: Concepts, Calculations and Context (Burkholder, Church & Wieman), Fermi Press premium edition.
Concept
Figure 4.2: the same beam and same two extinguishers can balance or not depending on where they sit. The force ledger (ΣF = 0) is blind to that difference; the twist ledger (weight × distance) is what changes.
Serves
Distinguishing translational equilibrium from rotational equilibrium. The force sum stays 0 in every arrangement of the level beam; only the torque ledger tips.
Inquiry
Slide an extinguisher outward and watch: which ledger changed, and which stayed put? Where in the force equation does position appear?
Misconception
That moving a weight along the beam changes the support’s normal force Np. While the beam stays level it does not — Np = 2Wf + Wb wherever they sit.

Pedagogy principles applied

Guided Inquiry

▼

1 · Two arrangements of the same beam

The same beam, the same mount and the same two fire extinguishers appear twice: balanced in the top panel, unbalanced in the bottom one.

Every force arrow is identical between the two panels. The only thing that differs is where the extinguishers sit.

2 · The complete force diagram

One rigid plank rests on one mount, which touches the underside at a single point, so the beam can turn about that point. Two identical extinguishers stand on it, one each side, about 29 cm out. Each presses down with its weight Wf, drawn in crimson where it stands.

The beam’s own weight Wb acts through its middle, on the mount’s vertical line, and the mount pushes up with a single force Np, drawn in gold:

∑Fy = Np − 2Wf − Wb = 0

Not one distance appears in it.

3 · Predict: slide one outward

Both extinguishers weigh the same. If you slide the right extinguisher farther from the mount and leave the left one alone, what happens to the support force Np that the mount pushes up on the beam?

4 · Three sliders: two distances and a weight

Unlocked below — Left distance, Right distance and Weight of each extinguisher.

You are holding the beam level. Holding it level takes a twist, not an extra push, so the hold adds nothing to the force ledger. The arrows now scale with the numbers, and a measuring bar appears under the beam.

Drag a distance: the Np row flashes gold to show it did not change, and only the twist ledger moves. Drag the weight: every entry in the force ledger changes at once, and the twist ledger stays balanced whenever the two distances match.

5 · Which ledger moved?

After sliding an extinguisher outward, which of the two ledgers actually changed?

6 · Let go, and name the product

Unlocked — Let go of the beam and the two panel presets.

Make the two distances unequal, then press it. The beam is free to turn about the mount, so this stops being a statics problem: both ledgers freeze at their last held-level values, and while the beam turns the vertical forces no longer sum to zero. The side with the larger weight × distance goes down — never the heavier side, because the two extinguishers weigh the same.

That product, the force times its distance from the pivot, is called torque (Section 4.1). Full equilibrium needs both ledgers at zero: ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0. Press Finish to tuck this away and explore freely.

What did you just see?

▼

Work through the steps above; the controls arrive one at a time.

Force balance (translational equilibrium)
ΣFy = Np − 2Wf − Wb = 0
Positions of the extinguishers do not appear.
Torque about the mount (rotational equilibrium)
Στ = Wf·a − Wf·b
Zero only when a = b. This is where position enters.

The Physics

Same two extinguishers — the force equation that stays the same while the beam is level · what this sim shows, the physics behind it, and every control

01

At a glance

A flat beam rests on a single mount, and two identical fire extinguishers stand on it, one on each side. The sim keeps two ledgers for the beam, one for forces and one for twists. You choose where each extinguisher stands and how heavy it is, and you can let the beam go.

What you'll learn

  • Which forces act on a loaded beam that rests on one mount, and what each of them equals.
  • How a force's distance from the mount turns it into a twist.
  • What must hold for the beam to stay level, and what happens when it does not.
The apparatus: one beam, one mount, two extinguishers at distances a and b.

What's on screen

  • The beam on its mount, with the two red extinguishers standing on it.
  • Crimson arrows: the weights, pointing down where each weight acts.
  • Gold arrow: the push of the mount, pointing up.
  • Ledgers in the sidebar: a twist ledger and a force ledger, with a short comment under them.
See itStart with the opening scene: both extinguishers 29 cm from the mount, 8 N each. Watch for: the beam level on its mount, with 29 cm on both sides.

Fixed in the sim: the beam weighs Wb = 12.0 N and rests on the mount at its middle. The extinguishers are identical, so one slider sets both weights.

03

The mount's push Np equals 2Wf + Wb

Three forces pull down on the beam: its own weight Wb at the middle, and one weight Wf under each extinguisher. The mount touches the underside at one point and pushes up with a single force Np. A beam at rest has no net vertical force:

ΣFy = Np − 2Wf − Wb = 0
This is the force ledger. It has no distance in it, only weights.

With Wf = 8.0 N and Wb = 12.0 N, Np = 2 × 8.0 + 12.0 = 28.0 N, and the ledger sum reads 0.0 N. The up arrow is as long as the three down arrows put together.

See itUse the opening scene, with the force ledger open. Watch for: Np 28.0 N and sum of the forces 0.0 N.
04

Sliding an extinguisher changes no force

A weight is the same wherever the extinguisher stands, so no force on the list depends on position. Slide the right extinguisher from 29 cm out to 46 cm. Wf is still 8.0 N, Wb is still 12.0 N, and Np is still 28.0 N. The mount carries the same three weights as before.

This holds while you keep the beam level. Holding it level calls for a twist, which adds a turning effect but no vertical push, so the force ledger is unaffected.

Changing the weight is different. Raise Wf to 14 N and every entry changes: Np = 2 × 14 + 12.0 = 40.0 N.

See itSlide the right extinguisher out to 46 cm. Watch for: Np 28.0 N and sum 0.0 N, unmoved from before.
See itRaise the weight of each extinguisher to 14 N. Watch for: Np 40.0 N, with each Wf row reading 14.0 N.
05

The twist ledger is weight × distance

A force turns the beam about the mount by an amount that grows with its distance from the mount. The sim measures the twist of each extinguisher as Wf × distance, in N·cm. The beam's weight and the mount's push act on the mount itself, at zero distance, so they add no twist.

At the opening scene, the left twist is 8.0 × 29 = 232 N·cm and the right twist is 232 N·cm, so left minus right is 0. Slide the right one out to 46 cm. Its twist becomes 8.0 × 46 = 368 N·cm, and the difference is 232 − 368 = −136 N·cm. The minus sign means the right side has the larger twist, which is clockwise.

Unlike the force ledger, this one changes whenever a distance changes.

See itKeep the right extinguisher at 46 cm, with the twist ledger open. Watch for: right 368 N·cm and left minus right −136 N·cm.
06

A level beam needs both ledgers at zero

A beam on a mount can fail in two ways. It could move bodily, or it could turn. Staying level with nothing holding it therefore needs two conditions together:

ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0
Force balance (translational) and twist balance about the mount (rotational).

The force ledger reads 0 in every arrangement of the level beam, so it cannot tell a balanced beam from an unbalanced one. The twist ledger can. With equal weights, Στ = Wfa − Wfb = Wf(a − b), which is zero only when a = b. The weight does not matter, only the match of the two distances.

With unequal weights the condition is W₁a = W₂b. A lighter weight can balance a heavier one by standing farther out, as on a seesaw. The sim keeps the weights equal, so it shows only the case a = b.

See itPut both extinguishers at 40 cm. Watch for: both twists reading 320 N·cm, and left minus right 0 N·cm.
07

Let go, and the larger twist wins

Release the beam with a ≠ b and it turns toward the side with the larger Wf × distance. It is not the heavier side that goes down, because the two extinguishers weigh the same. With the extinguishers at 19 cm and 46 cm, the right twist is 368 N·cm against 152 N·cm, so the right side goes down.

Once the beam turns, the problem is no longer statics. The sim freezes both ledgers at the values they had while the beam was level, because while it turns the vertical forces no longer sum to zero. In the sim the extinguishers also slide down the slope.

See itPut the extinguishers at 19 cm and 46 cm, then let go. Watch for: the right side swinging down, and the ledgers frozen at their old values.
08

Where it matters

  • Seesaws. A heavy child balances a light one by sitting closer to the pivot, so that the products weight × distance match.
  • Beam balances and steelyards. An unknown weight is found from a known weight and the two distances.
  • Cranes. A counterweight is placed so that its twist cancels the twist of the load about the tower.
  • Shelves and bridges. The support must carry the total load, and it must also resist the twist of loads placed away from it.
09

Summary

In one line. A beam resting on one mount is held up by forces and turned by twists, and the sim keeps one ledger for each.

Key points

  • Force ledger: Np = 2Wf + Wb, with no distance in it.
  • Twist ledger: each extinguisher gives Wf × distance.
  • Sliding an extinguisher changes the twist ledger and leaves the force ledger alone.
  • When released, the beam turns toward the larger twist, not the heavier side.

Common mix-ups

  • "Moving a weight outward makes the mount push harder." Np depends on the weights only, while the beam is level.
  • "Equal weights always balance." They balance only at equal distances from the mount.
  • "The heavier side goes down." The side with the larger weight × distance goes down.

Things to try on your own

  • Raise Wf to 20 N and work out Np before you read it.
  • Find another pair of distances that gives a left minus right difference of −136 N·cm at 8 N.
  • Put the left extinguisher at 0 cm and the right at 29 cm, then let go.
